title: We put a survivorship-free US equities lake behind a free API: 59k symbols, 35k of them dead, 101M daily rows. Here is exactly what is in it and what is broken.
author: Must_Dragonfruit
selftext:
Most free price data quietly deletes the losers. Backtest on it and every bankruptcy, delisting and buyout has already left your universe, so your numbers come out better than the world was. We got tired of that and built our own lake. It feeds the paper-trading bots on [engo.capital](http://engo.capital), and anyone with a free account key can read it. This post is the inventory, including the parts that are wrong.

**What is in it (as of 2026-09-04)**

* **Symbol book:** 58,908 US symbols, 23,999 active, 34,909 delisted. One call gets the whole book as parquet.
* **Daily history, archive (**`us_eod`**):** 101,394,171 adjusted daily rows, 2000-01-03 to 2026-08-04. Splits and dividends adjusted. Delisted names included, so yes, you can price Enron. Frozen at 2026-08-04 because the upstream vendor entitlement lapsed. It says so in every response.
* **Daily history, forward (**`us_eod_native`**):** 11,173 listed symbols from 2026-08-04 onward, appended every trading morning (through 2026-09-03 right now). Raw Polygon grouped bars chained into a total-return index in-house, with Polygon corporate actions and Alpaca as an independent action witness. A symbol with a source disagreement is quarantined for that session instead of guessed. Listed names only, no OTC.
* **Point-in-time S&P 500 membership:** 817 join/leave records. Our own audit only trusts it from 2018-06-30; before that the reconstructed count falls under our 450-member floor. Strict mode returns 422 for those dates instead of a thin universe.
* **Corporate actions:** about 7,300 symbols, 254,285 events. Splits keep numerator and denominator apart so a 1-for-8 cannot get flipped. Dividends come both adjusted and as-paid. One static snapshot from 2026-07-27, not point-in-time.
* **Value-quality screens:** per symbol, live, over the bars you would actually get. Plus a book-level sample: 300 symbols, 16.6% flagged (95% CI 12.7 to 21.4). Most flags are one dataset-wide defect: the archive pairs raw open/high/low with an adjusted close in the same row. Nothing is rewritten. You get the value and the reason.
* **Fundamentals as filed:** SEC company facts for 7,874 symbols, snapshotted 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-02, filtered by filing date on read, so a later restatement cannot leak into a historical test.
* **Futures:** ES and NQ daily 2010-06 to 2026-06 (112k rows), plus 19.9M minute rows, 8.9M trades and 23.7M depth rows in partitions. Honest part: exactly one NQ session has trades and depth together, and one depth partition holds 1 row against 26M at the provider. The inventory endpoint tells you this before you download anything.
* **Panels with receipts:** up to 100 symbols and 250k rows per call, JSON or parquet, each with a receipt: manifest hash, actual dates, missing symbols, adjustment basis, universe status. Strict by default. Miss one symbol and the whole call fails naming it, unless you opt into partial.

**How to read it**

Free account at [engo.capital](http://engo.capital), mint a key, then `GET /api/v1/lake/...` with `Authorization: Bearer`. Docs at engo.capital/wiki. Everything is pyarrow, pandas and DuckDB friendly. Research use.

**What is broken or missing, in order of how much it hurts**

1. Post-2026-08-04 prices for OTC and delisted names. The archive froze and the native feed is listed-only.
2. Point-in-time corporate actions. Ours is a snapshot; a restatement overwrites the past.
3. S&P 500 membership before 2018 that is dense enough to trust.
4. Historical option chains with bid and ask. We have none worth the name.
5. Insider transactions, calibrated news-event labels, and futures microstructure beyond one session.

If you have any of these, know a vendor whose terms allow it, or want to check our numbers, say so here or email [tom@engo.capital](mailto:tom@engo.capital). Corrections welcome. The whole point of the lake is that it ships the honesty with the prices.
